Variants.Content: Deposition, which asserts that a ruler has lost his qualifications to continue to rule, is one of the most dangerous forms of political language. It may come from jurisprudence, war, or a collective turn; once it is spoken, everyone must answer again whether their allegiance is to the person, the crown, or the order.

Entry Deposition Deposition, which asserts that a ruler has lost his qualifications to continue to rule, is one of the most dangerous forms of political language. It may come from jurisprudence, war, or a collective turn; once it is spoken, everyone must answer again whether their allegiance is to the person, the crown, or the order. They start by asking who is obligated, who is protected, and who will seek justice after a breach of contract.

Entry Deposition Deposition, which asserts that a ruler has lost his qualifications to continue to rule, is one of the most dangerous forms of political language. It may come from jurisprudence, war, or a collective turn; once it is spoken, everyone must answer again whether their allegiance is to the person, the crown, or the order. For them, what really matters is whether the orders can arrive, whether the roads are safe, and whether the food and pay can be received on time.

It may come from jurisprudence, war, or a collective turn; once it is spoken, everyone must answer again whether their allegiance is to the person, the crown, or the order. What is remembered is not who spoke the loudest in the hall, but which rule saved the family from starvation, conscription, or endless fighting.
